title: Petroleum Retail Marketing Sites and Franchise Acts repealed; Oilcode introduced
summary: From 1 March 2007 the limits on oil majors running retail sites directly were repealed and a mandatory Oilcode governed fuel reselling.

commenced.what: Sites and Franchise Acts repealed; Oilcode commenced

direction_rationale: Removing limits on direct retailing by refiners allows more vertical integration, which can lower costs or foreclose independents.
comparison: Local share of sites run by majors (needs station data)

verified.notes: Date and assent from the as-made Act on the Federal Register.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Repealed limits on oil refiners running service stations directly, and introduced a mandatory Oilcode for fuel reselling. Refiners can integrate into retail, which may lower costs or squeeze independents.

marks.reason: Removes limits on how many sites refiners could operate directly.

responsible.note: The Oilcode is an industry code under the Competition and Consumer Act 2010, which Treasury administers.

history.what: The Oilcode was remade as the Competition and Consumer (Industry Codes—Oil) Regulations 2017 (registered 14 March 2017).
